name: Ouroboros: Generating Longer Drafts Phrase by Phrase for Faster Speculative Decoding
problem: Under the draft-then-verify framing, DRAFTING efficiency - not verification - is the bottleneck capping total speculative-decoding speedup.
mechanism: Draft PHRASES rather than tokens, training-free. A second (draft) model is used to generate a whole draft phrase autoregressively, but the phrases are then processed so that the actual token drafting is parallelised - the draft model's phrase-level outputs are fed through the target model's layers as a batch, converting sequential drafting into a parallel one, while lengthening drafts at no extra training cost. Accepts a given prefix of the draft and continues, keeping the modified rejection-sampling exactness property.
speedup_reported: Up to 2.8x OVER SPECULATIVE DECODING and 3.9x over vanilla decoding, without fine-tuning either the draft or target models, on typical text-generation tasks. Note the two different denominators: 2.8x is the improvement over an already-good speculative-decoding baseline, 3.9x is over plain decoding. The 2.8x is the number that actually characterises the contribution.
notes:
ADOPTION: research-only - not in vLLM, llama.cpp, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM as of verification. VENUE: EMNLP 2024 per the arXiv comment field; Semantic Scholar was rate-limited at verification time so this rests on the arXiv comment alone. Reading note for the cost model: this paper attacks the DRAFT side, whereas EAGLE/MagicDec attack the VERIFY side, which is why their speedups do not compose automatically - and why the honest way to read this record is as an attack on the same bottleneck from the opposite side. There is also a confusingly-named sibling, Ouroboros-2 (online speculative decoding, a different paper and a different mechanism), which was searched for and could NOT be confirmed against the arXiv API under any title query attempted; it is deliberately not recorded here rather than recorded with a guessed identifier.
